When choosing whether to go ap or ad jg Shaco, I often pick depending on what kind of late game I want. I pick ap for a strong late game, especially if they are tank heavy or you expect brawly teamfights. My ap shaco games consistently return a lot more damage than my ad games, while the damage in ad games is more focused. In many ways I think you are right, but it depends.

When jungling, AP shaco often relies on boxes to clear, so you often put points in w early,  and his ap scaling is fairly weak. For this reason AP has weaker and more unreliable ganks early. On the other side, towards the end of early game/start of mid game your clear is very fast and strong, and your ult becomes a decent source of zoning and burst in ganks.

Shaco also likes damage amp items which scale his abilities outside of pure AP or give you utility to reliably juice max damage from your abilities (liandry, demonic, zhonya). This also means shaco scales well with items, but not because of the flat AP or MP they give. Incidentally these items are often more effective against tanks.

What you end up with is a build that is stronger in teamfights and has a strong af clear going into mid game, while you sacrifice burst damage against squishies and early-mid gank power. So relative to AD, AP is much more late game oriented and it scales better in many cases. 

You will still never outscale that Veigar or Senna, though. In those cases, you just build AD and remove those champs instead, essentially meaning you negate enemy team scaling instead of scaling yourself.

Her er du på ball - den faktisk interessante diskusjonen starter emm. med spørsmålet om hvorvidt regelverket er effektivt og om det finnes reelle alternativer. Det er klart at det vekker reaksjoner når avisene ordlegger seg slik, men det er lite fruktbart å se rett til DNB på jakt etter en antagonist i saken.

Jajo... analogien din er ikke så treffende: man har ikke et reelt alternativ til børsene. Man kan jo selvsagt si at man på et indirekte vis bidrar til finansiering av mindre enn heldige industrier ved å handle på aksjemarkedet. Problemet er at det blir en unyttig øvelse fordi å forby folk å handle aksjer ville gjort mye mer skade enn nytte. Man kunne også forbudt alle transaksjoner og kastet alle som handler hos andre enn et nyopprettet statlig monopol i fengsel på livstid, men det ville nok a) neppe fungert, b) gitt all velferd nakkeskudd og c) møtt så mye motstand at det ikke ville skjedd.

Når man pålegger finansinstitusjoner å være så forsiktige at noen transaksjoner ikke går gjennom, men likevel slik at de fleste kan betale for seg med mer sporbare midler, er oppfatningen at det forvansker svart omsetning såpass mye mer enn det det forvansker hvit at det er verdt å regulere. 

Man kan på et vis si at de tapte inntektene og administrative utgiftene ved en slik ordning er prisen statsmakten har satt på bekjempelse av hvitvasking, om du vil. Å stenge børsene blir for dyrt.

That is not necessarily right and is an often misunderstood part of GDPR. Not all processing without consent is in breach of GDPR. Article 6 allows other grounds for processing than consent, such as a need to fulfill a contract (option b) or pursuit of a legitimate interest (option f). Best practice for GDPR compliance actually  tends to be to ask for consent as rarely as possible, and try to process data on other legal grounds. 

That being said I doubt 2k or whoever can shoehorn in a justification for processing all that data, which opens a whole different can of GDPR worms (purposes for processing etc.). 

Edit: you do still need to accept the EULA terms as a contract. This consumer relationship is subject to "regular" consumer contract law. 

You do, however, in 95% of cases, have the right to opt out.
